question: What is the medical term for high blood pressure?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hypertension**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypertension** is the medical term for high blood pressure.
 
• It is a condition where the **force of the blood against the artery walls is too high**.
 
• Hypertension is often referred to as a **silent killer** because it may not show any symptoms for years.
 
• It can lead to serious health complications like **heart disease, stroke, and kidney failure**.
 
• Common causes include **genetic factors, poor diet, lack of physical activity, and stress**.
 
• Management includes **lifestyle changes** such as a balanced diet, regular exercise, and medications as prescribed by healthcare providers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hypotension**__

 __
 
• **Hypotension** is the medical term for low blood pressure.
 
• It can cause symptoms like **dizziness, fainting, and fatigue**.
 
• Severe hypotension can be life-threatening, leading to shock.
 
 
 
• **Hyperglycemia**__
 __
 
• **Hyperglycemia** is the medical term for high blood sugar levels.
 
• It is commonly associated with **diabetes**.
 
• Symptoms include **increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue**.
 
 
 
• **Hypoglycemia**__
 
 
• **Hypoglycemia** refers to low blood sugar levels.
 
• It can cause symptoms such as **shakiness, sweating, confusion, and irritability**.
 
• If untreated, it can lead to **seizures, unconsciousness, or even death**.
